messages:
IncidentBot: P0 alert — elevated generation latency and intermittent 5xx from eu-west-fastgen pool starting 2026-03-15T08:12:34Z. Error rate ~12% over last 5m, tail lat spikes. Trigger: service:fastgen-eu, metric:latency_99p, threshold breach. Paging oncall: @alex m :rotating_light:
Alex M: I’m on it. pulling logs and checking autoscale. paging in ops channel and grabbing a second pair of eyes. ETA 5m.
Priya S: I see duplicate KV cache misses trending up in the same time window. could be cache eviction thrash after the 03:00 rollout.
Jamal K: Can you paste the query for the cache metrics? I want to correlate with GPU memory OOMs.
Alex M: running the queries now —
Alex M: ```
# kibana query
index:fastgen-logs AND env:eu-west AND level:error AND message:/KVCache/ AND @timestamp:[now-10m TO now]
```
Alex M: results show ~430 KVCache misses and occasional gpu OOMs on node fastgen-eu-12.
Emily T: Is this affecting embeddings or only generation? Customer impact?
Alex M: generation only. embeddings and inference routing still OK. initial triage: increased 99p due to repeated kernel restarts on node 12 after a quantization kernel regression from last night’s model push.
Charlie R: tagging runbook: please follow the EU-generation degradation playbook, steps 1-4. I’ll take statuspage copy review.
Alex M: drafting initial status page update — putting draft here for quick review before publish (keeping it customer-facing):
Alex M: ```
Status: Investigating
Service: Text generation (eu-west)
Impact: Customers in eu-west may experience increased latency and occasional failed generation requests.
Start time: 2026-03-15T08:12 UTC
What we’re doing: Our on-call engineers are investigating root cause and routing traffic away from impacted hosts. No customer data access or exfiltration detected.
Next update: within 30 minutes or as needed.
```
Priya S: good start. Suggest clarifying "failed generation requests" -> "requests returning 5xx errors" and add a note about any affected SDKs/versions if known.
Jamal K: add a line: "We are temporarily shifting traffic to healthy replicas in other EU capacity while we remediate" — helps set expectations.
Emily T: +1 and please add "no action required from customers" if that's true.
Alex M: updated draft with tweaks — dropping internal jargon and adding the routing note. new copy below:```
Status: Investigating
Service: Text generation (eu-west)
Impact: Some customers in the eu-west region may see elevated latency (high 99th percentile) and intermittent 5xx errors for text generation requests.
Start time: 2026-03-15T08:12 UTC
What we’re doing: Engineering has identified a subset of hosts with kernel restarts following a recent model kernel change. We are shifting traffic away from impacted hosts to healthy replicas and rolling back the kernel change on the affected pool.
Customer action: No action required. We will post updates as mitigation progresses.
Next update: within 30 minutes.
```
Charlie R: clean. I’d remove the words "kernel change" — too technical, maybe "a recent runtime change". Also confirm whether a rollback is safe to call out. If it's in-flight, say "we are rolling back" is fine.
Alex M: ok changed to "a recent runtime change". publishing now. @statuspage-bot please create incident and publish initial update.
statuspage-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-456). Initial update published to status.redwood.ai: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-456 :white_check_mark:
Emily T: great — can someone flag customers with active SLAs or currently active long-running jobs so support can proactively notify?
Jamal K: I’ll pull the active job list and tag affected account ids in support queue. sending to #support-escalations.
Alex M: mitigation actions: 1) traffic shifted off fastgen-eu-12 2) rolling back runtime change on pool fastgen-eu 3) monitoring for kernel restarts post-rollback.
Alex M: posting periodic update for statuspage (15:40 UTC):
Alex M: ```
Update 1 (2026-03-15T08:27 UTC): We have shifted traffic away from the affected hosts and initiated a rollback of the recent runtime change on the eu-west generation pool. Error rates have decreased from ~12% to ~3% in the last 10 minutes. Engineering continues to monitor and will provide another update in 30 minutes.
```
Priya S: Nice, can we add the metric delta: 12% -> 3% so customers have context? already included ;). Consider adding note that we’ll be keeping throttles off to avoid retries.
Charlie R: small edit: "we will continue to monitor and keep the API available; automated retries will be suppressed to avoid compounding load" — avoid telling customers to retry.
Alex M: updated and republished. statuspage-bot: Update posted to INC-2026-456.
statuspage-bot: (internal note) Incident assigned to SRE: alex m, backup: jamal k.
Emily T: Support notifications queued — sending proactive emails to accounts with >1min active jobs. template:``` 
Subject: Notice - Temporary degradation of text generation in eu-west
Body: Hi <Customer>,
We’re investigating elevated latency and intermittent failures for text generation in our eu-west region. Our engineers have shifted traffic and are rolling back a recent runtime change. No action required — we’ll follow up when resolved. Apologies for the disruption.
```
Jamal K: sent proactive messages for 24 accounts flagged by job filter. support ticket IDs attached.
Alex M: rolling back completed on fastgen-eu pool at 08:45 UTC. kernel restarts stopped on node 12. continuing to monitor. publishing update:```
Update 2 (2026-03-15T08:46 UTC): Rollback completed. Error rates reduced to baseline (~0.2%). Affected hosts have stabilized and normal traffic flow restored for the eu-west generation pool. We will keep monitoring and will resolve the incident once stability is confirmed for 30m.
```
Charlie R: good. add a line "no data exposure" to reassure.
Alex M: added and republished. statuspage-bot: Update posted to INC-2026-456.
statuspage-bot: (public) Incident status changed to: Monitoring.
Emily T: Support closed the high-priority outreach loop; only 2 customers requested follow-up — both escalated to CSM.
Jamal K: monitoring window passed 30m with stable metrics. preparing resolved notice.
Alex M: final resolved draft:```
Status: Resolved
Service: Text generation (eu-west)
Impact: Some customers experienced elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors between 2026-03-15T08:12 UTC and 2026-03-15T08:46 UTC.
What happened: A recent runtime change introduced a kernel behavior regression in the eu-west generation pool which caused kernel restarts on a subset of hosts.
What we did: We shifted traffic off affected hosts and rolled back the runtime change. Hosts were monitored until metrics returned to baseline.
Customer action: No action required. If you continue to see issues, please contact support.
Next steps: Post-incident RCA to follow; we will update the RCA link here when available. No data access or exfiltration occurred.
```
Alex M: published resolved notice. statuspage-bot: Incident INC-2026-456 marked Resolved and final update posted. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-456 :tada:
Charlie R: please add RCA link when ready and mark followups for the release that introduced the runtime change.
Priya S: will own the RCA write-up, timeline, and the code rollback PR review.
Alex M: thanks team — nice quick cycle. closing thread. :slightly_smiling_face:
